newsitem.title: USA: CME hog calls mixed, pork bellies higher.
newsitem.headline: CME hog calls mixed, pork bellies higher.

text.p: Early calls on CME hog futures ranged from 0.200 cent per lb higher to 0.100 lower while pork bellies were expected to open 0.250 to 0.500 cent higher, livestock analysts said.

Although some analysts look for early resistance in hog futures on concern over the large premium futures hold to cash hog prices, steady to higher cash hog calls Thursday should provide support. Packers are curbing slaughter operations but a lack of hog marketings was pushing cash prices higher. To keep production lines working packers were being forced to pay up for the limited supply of cash hogs Thursday despite negative profit margins, analysts said.
The Taiwan pork ban also remained overall supportive.

The latest reports from Taiwan have 18 percent of their hog farms infected with the foot-and-mouth disease with official projections that over 3.54 million of Taiwan's 14.0 million hogs have been or would be destroyed.
The Taiwan problem and expected increased pork exports to previous Taiwan customers should continue to offset slow domestic demand for pork, analysts said.

Pork belly futures have already been influenced by the Taiwan pork ban with Japan buying U.S. bellies. This and rising cash pork belly prices were expected to boost pork belly futures early after values in that pit set new contract highs in all frozen contracts Wednesday, analysts said.
Cash bellies ranged up to $88 per cwt Wednesday, the highest level since August 16.

This week's reduced slaughter pace and much-lighter-than- year-ago pace of storings as well as strong technical signals should offset any concern that high cash prices will be hurting domestic demand, they added.
